About one in five Australians were expected to celebrate in 2024, spending around $450 million, per Australian Retailers Association data reported by the ABC; no official ABS figure exists.

faqs.question: Is Halloween a public holiday in Australia?
faqs.answer: No. 31 October is not on the Fair Work Ombudsman's 2026 or 2027 public holiday lists for any state or territory, so shops, offices and schools keep normal hours. The nearest real holidays are Melbourne Cup Day in Victoria (Tuesday 3 November 2026, Tuesday 2 November 2027) and Recreation Day in parts of Tasmania.

faqs.question: Do kids actually go trick-or-treating in Australia?
faqs.answer: Yes, in many suburbs, but only at houses that opt in. Retail data reported by the ABC in 2024 had 38% of Australians planning to buy lollies for trick-or-treaters, and most of the knocking happens in daylight or early dusk.

faqs.question: What does an orange balloon on a letterbox mean at Halloween?
faqs.answer: It means the house is taking part and trick-or-treaters are welcome to knock. University of Sydney professor Ellen Garbarino describes it as a local Australian signal; a dark house with no balloon or decorations is best left alone.

faqs.question: Why do some Australians dislike Halloween?
faqs.answer: Mostly because they see it as an American import pushed by retailers. A 2013 Medical Journal of Australia article argued the confectionery industry campaigned to establish it here in the early 1990s, and raised concerns about marketing lollies to children.

faqs.question: When did Halloween start in Australia?
faqs.answer: Earlier than most people think in a few places. Ravenswood in north Queensland has held a Halloween ball probably since at least the mid-1870s, according to local historian Ray Holyoak, while the suburban trick-or-treat version grew from the 1990s onwards.

faqs.question: What time do kids trick-or-treat in Australia?
faqs.answer: Usually late afternoon to early evening, while it is still light. On 31 October the sun sets at about 7:21 pm in Sydney and 7:53 pm in Melbourne (daylight saving time), but around 6:05 pm in Brisbane and 6:40 pm in Perth, which do not use daylight saving.

faqs.question: Can you buy pumpkins for Halloween in Australia?
faqs.answer: Yes. The Australian Retailers Association expected more than 1 million kilograms of pumpkins to be sold for Halloween 2024, despite the festival falling in spring. We found no reliable source on which varieties are in season in October.

faqs.question: What is the weather like for Halloween in Sydney?
faqs.answer: Mild. The Bureau of Meteorology's long-term averages for Sydney (Observatory Hill) put the October mean maximum at 22.2 °C, so costumes made for a cold northern autumn can feel hot in the afternoon.

faqs.question: Is Halloween on a weekend in 2026 and 2027?
faqs.answer: Yes, both years. Halloween falls on Saturday 31 October 2026 and Sunday 31 October 2027, so trick-or-treating does not clash with a school night.

faqs.question: How do I send a Halloween message from Australia to family in the UK or US?
faqs.answer: Send it in your evening and it lands in their morning: 7 pm in Sydney on 31 October is 8 am in London and 4 am in New York the same day. A Halloween card link works in a phone or laptop browser with no app, and 48.3% of SubhSandesh pages are opened on a phone (platform-wide).

# Halloween in Australia: Why It Feels Different Down Under

Halloween in Australia is celebrated on 31 October, but as a newer, smaller and sunnier version of the American night. It falls in spring, trick-or-treating mostly happens in daylight, and it is not a public holiday in any state or territory. More than one in five Australians were expected to join in during 2024, spending about $450 million on costumes, decorations and lollies, according to [Australian Retailers Association figures reported by the ABC (30 October 2024)](https://www.abc.net.au/news/2024-10-30/australians-look-for-fun-and-frivolity-with-budget-halloween/104518538). The next two dates are Saturday 31 October 2026 and Sunday 31 October 2027.

Greeting someone overseas on the night? On SubhSandesh, 48.3% of shared pages get opened on a phone and a page draws 11.1 views on average, measured across every template rather than Halloween alone.

Below: who takes part, why it caught on, what spring changes, street etiquette, and a US and UK comparison.

## How many Australians celebrate Halloween?

Roughly one in five, from a retail survey rather than an official count. The ABC's 2024 report quotes ARA data: 38% of Australians planned to buy lollies for trick-or-treaters, 37% costumes and 32% home decorations, and the largest group of celebrators was aged 35 to 59.

Those are forecasts from a retailers' body. We found no Australian Bureau of Statistics series on Halloween participation or spending, so every Australian Halloween number, including these, is a survey or a forecast.

An older baseline exists. A 2013 article in the [Medical Journal of Australia by Gillian Porter and Nathan Grills](https://www.mja.com.au/journal/2013/199/8/dark-side-halloween-marketing-unhealthy-products-our-children) cited market figures showing a quarter of Australians then planned to celebrate. Different surveys, so read it as a steady minority with rising spending, not a boom.

## Why is Halloween a thing in Australia?

Because two stories are both true: an old Celtic custom that arrived with 19th-century settlers, and a 1990s sales push that made it a suburban street event. Which one you hear depends on who is telling it.

### The old thread: a gold-town ball since the 1870s

Ravenswood, a north Queensland gold-mining town of about 300 people, holds a Halloween ball that draws around 500. Local historian Ray Holyoak [told ABC North Queensland in 2018](https://www.abc.net.au/news/2018-10-31/ravenswood-110-year-old-halloween-ball-keeps-town-alive/10447780) it has probably run since at least the mid-1870s, a tradition of Welsh and Anglo-Celtic miners rather than "some crass Americanism".

A photograph from about 1908 shows a cycle race under a Halloween banner on Macrossan Street. Today the ball raises about $10,000 a year for the town's state school.

### The commercial thread: confectioners in the 1990s

Porter and Grills, of the University of Melbourne's Nossal Institute for Global Health, write that the confectionery industry ran a media campaign in the early 1990s to establish Halloween in Australia. A 2002 US Confectionery Industry Export Program report still called progress slow and retailer support lacking.

Retailers caught up: in 2012, leading Australian supermarkets recorded increases of up to 30% in Halloween merchandise sales. The authors conclude: "We are tricking ourselves if we believe that we have adopted the treat of Halloween as a cultural event of our own volition."

### The scholarly middle

University of Sydney religious studies professor Carole Cusack [traces the customs](https://www.sydney.edu.au/news-opinion/news/2025/10/21/halloween-in-australia-how-an-irish-tradition-became-a-uniquely-local-celebration.html) to Scottish and Irish folklore, carried to America by Irish famine migrants in the 1840s. So "it's an American import" is half right: the doorstep version was sold in by confectioners and retailers, while the older custom came with Celtic settlers.

## What changes when Halloween falls in spring?

Daylight is the big difference. New South Wales, Victoria, South Australia, Tasmania and the ACT start daylight saving on the first Sunday in October (4 October 2026, 3 October 2027), so the sun sets late on 31 October. We computed these sunset times with the NOAA solar-position equations, accurate to about two minutes:

- Sydney 7:21 pm AEDT
- Melbourne 7:53 pm AEDT
- Adelaide 7:43 pm ACDT
- Hobart 7:52 pm AEDT
- Brisbane 6:05 pm AEST (no daylight saving)
- Perth 6:40 pm AWST (no daylight saving)
- Darwin 6:46 pm ACST (no daylight saving)

University of Sydney marketing professor Ellen Garbarino told the ABC that with daylight saving "the scary vibe doesn't work as well at five in the afternoon on a sunny day". In her account the Australian night is more about socialising than fright.

The weather is mild too. The [Bureau of Meteorology's long-term averages for Sydney (Observatory Hill)](https://www.bom.gov.au/climate/averages/tables/cw_066062.shtml) put the October mean maximum at 22.2 °C and November's at 23.7 °C. Light layers and sunscreen beat a full-face mask for a 4 pm start.

Pumpkins are not missing, despite the common claim: the ARA expected more than 1 million kilograms to sell for Halloween 2024. We found no source on which varieties are in season in October.

## Halloween 2026 and 2027 dates in Australia

Halloween is Saturday 31 October 2026 and Sunday 31 October 2027. Neither date appears on the Fair Work Ombudsman's 2026 or 2027 public holiday lists for any state or territory, so trading and work hours stay normal.

Two real holidays follow it. Melbourne Cup Day is Tuesday 3 November 2026 and Tuesday 2 November 2027 in Victoria, though some regional areas pick another date. Parts of Tasmania take Recreation Day on Monday 2 November 2026 and Monday 1 November 2027. Both years put Halloween on a weekend, so trick-or-treaters are not out on a school night.

## Trick-or-treat etiquette in Australian suburbs

It is opt-in, and the signal is on the letterbox. Garbarino, in the University of Sydney's October 2025 explainer, describes houses tying orange balloons to the letterbox to show they are taking part, with residents often sitting out the front in daylight. She calls the night a social contract among mostly strangers that only works if everyone plays their role.

These rules follow from that contract. Many of your neighbours will not be playing:

- Knock only where there is a sign: an orange balloon, a decorated porch or a lit lantern.
- A dark house with nothing out the front means no.
- Aim for daylight or early dusk; in Sydney that is before about 7:20 pm.
- Take one or two lollies, say thanks, and stay off gardens.
- Small children walk with an adult; older kids go in a group with a charged phone.
- Handing out? Keep stickers as a non-food option, since the MJA authors flag extra risk for children with food allergies.
- Respect a "no trick-or-treaters" note on the gate.

Road safety matters more than any costume. The [NSW Centre for Road Safety](https://www.transport.nsw.gov.au/roadsafety/pedestrians/staying-safe) advises against crossing between parked cars or at the front or back of buses, and recommends bright, light-coloured or reflective clothing wherever visibility is poor. Practise its Stop, Look, Listen, Think routine at the first kerb; drivers should slow down.

## Halloween in Australia vs the US and UK

The table compares the three countries on the points that most change the night. Sunset times are our computed values for 31 October 2026.

| Country | Season and sunset on 31 Oct | Trick-or-treat norm | Public holiday? |
|---|---|---|---|
| Australia | Spring; 7:21 pm in Sydney (AEDT); Oct mean max 22.2 °C | Opt-in, mostly daylight, orange balloon on the letterbox | No, in any state or territory |
| United States | Autumn; 5:55 pm in New York (EDT) | Widespread, after dark, house to house | No, not a federal holiday |
| United Kingdom | Autumn; 4:37 pm in London (GMT, clocks back 25 Oct) | A minority practice, after dark; Bonfire Night on 5 Nov competes | No |

The takeaway is daylight. Sydney keeps the sun 2 hours 44 minutes longer than London and 1 hour 26 minutes longer than New York, which is why Sydney's night reads as a street party, not a fright night.

## Sending a Halloween greeting to family overseas

Your evening is their morning. At 7 pm in Sydney on Saturday 31 October 2026 it is 8 am in London, 4 am in New York and 1:30 pm in Delhi, the same calendar day, and the offsets repeat in 2027.

For a grandparent in Glasgow or a cousin in Toronto, the [interactive Halloween card](https://subhsandesh.in/happy-halloween) offers a family mode. You add a short letter, as many as six photos and a word to carve, then share a private link over WhatsApp or text. On their screen a small haunted house waits: they rap on the door three times, carve the pumpkin until your word lights up, clear misted portraits to reveal your photos, and read your letter by torchlight in the attic.

Choosing family or kids rewrites the final question and the licence wording. For young cousins, the Kids tone keeps things spooky-cute, with round blushing ghosts and nothing gory or sudden. The finale is a Boo License sized 1080×1920 for an Instagram Story, stamped "Valid every 31 October, forever", and an email reaches you when they first reply.

A link suits a relative abroad who lives on their phone, and 90.9% of started SubhSandesh pages end up published and shared (platform-wide). Last-minute is normal too. The closest festival we have measured is Raksha Bandhan 2026, a different occasion with only 89 pages: 49.4% were made on the day and the median lead time was zero days.

If they would rather hear you, the [premium Halloween page](https://subhsandesh.in/happy-halloween-premium) carries a voice note (60 seconds at most), as many as 12 photos and an optional unlock time. Before that moment the link shows just their name and a countdown, so it can open at breakfast in London.

### When to skip the Halloween link

Sometimes a link is the wrong gift. In these cases we would send something else:

- An older relative who sees Halloween as an American import may find a pumpkin page odd; a phone call lands better.
- A grandparent who never opens links will enjoy a posted card more.
- Every screen is in English, so a non-English-speaking relative may struggle.
- It greets one person; it cannot invite a street or run a costume party.
- If you live in the same suburb, a bag of lollies at the gate beats any link.

## Sources

- Australian Retailers Association data, reported by Georgie Hewson, ABC News, 30 October 2024
- Nathalie Fernbach, Gold mining town's Halloween tradition still alive after 110 years, ABC News, 31 October 2018
- Gillian P Porter and Nathan J Grills, The dark side to Halloween, Medical Journal of Australia 199(8), 21 October 2013
- University of Sydney, What Halloween means for Australia, 21 October 2025
- Bureau of Meteorology, Climate statistics for Sydney (Observatory Hill), undated
- Transport for NSW Centre for Road Safety, Staying safe as a pedestrian, undated

structuralLimitations: Brief/prompt said the Australian opt-in decoration signal is a 'lolly bag'. The only source found (University of Sydney, Garbarino, 2025) says ORANGE BALLOONS on the letterbox; the post uses balloons and makes no lolly-bag claim.

Prompt framing 'no pumpkins in season' is contradicted by ARA data via the ABC (over 1 million kg of pumpkins expected to sell for Halloween 2024). No source on October pumpkin varieties/seasonality was found, so the body says so and makes no seasonality claim.

Participation/spending: no ABS or other government series exists. Figures are ARA forecasts reported by the ABC (retail.org.au returned 403, so the primary release was not read) and the MJA's 2013 'quarter of Australians' market figure. McCrindle's 2011/2012 surveys (26% planned to celebrate; 45% of non-celebrators cited 'American tradition') were read but not cited: stale and a top-5 SERP page.

Public holidays verified on fairwork.gov.au 2026 and 2027 public-holiday pages (no 31 October entry in any state; Melbourne Cup Tue 3 Nov 2026 / Tue 2 Nov 2027; Tas Recreation Day Mon 2 Nov 2026 / Mon 1 Nov 2027). Not linked, to stay within 6 outbound links; named in the body.

Sunset times are computed (NOAA general solar-position equations, zenith 90.833°, city-centre coordinates), not from BoM or Geoscience Australia; stated as computed in the body. Daylight-saving start (first Sunday of October: 4 Oct 2026, 3 Oct 2027; NSW, Vic, SA, Tas, ACT) and US/UK offsets (US DST ends 1 Nov 2026 / 7 Nov 2027; UK clocks back 25 Oct 2026 / 31 Oct 2027 at 02:00) are calendar-rule facts, not linked.

Peer-reviewed source: the MJA piece is a Perspective in a peer-reviewed journal, free to read on mja.com.au; it is the only scholarly source. Searches tried: findpapers 'Halloween Australia', 'Halloween Australian children trick-or-treating', 'Halloween southern hemisphere spring celebration', 'Halloween globalisation American holiday spread', 'Halloween Americanisation Australian culture'; Europe PMC TITLE:halloween AND australia. Shine & Shine 2016 (Australian Zoologist, Halloween and suburban fauna) is closed access with no abstract, so not cited. Staples et al. 2019 (JAMA Pediatr, US Halloween pedestrian deaths, PMC6583441) had no readable body (JAMA 403, PMC XML metadata only) and is a Batch 1 source, so not cited.

The Conversation (prompt suggestion) was checked: Whitaker 2019 'Hell, no! Halloween is not satanic' is Australian but about religious objections, not the rise of Halloween in Australia; the 2014 group-behaviour piece reports a US Chicago study. Neither was load-bearing, so theconversation.com is not cited.

University of Sydney and ABC 2024 are themselves in/near the SERP (sydney.edu.au is #1). They are not commercial competitors (a university and a public broadcaster), so citing them is allowed; the post's distinctive claims (MJA 1990s campaign, Ravenswood, sunset comparison, holiday neighbours) are not on any top-5 page.
